name: SWA Television Title
epitaph: The fed's own Wrestler Records page (27 August 2000) credits seven different wrestlers with one Television Title reign apiece — Donny “The Dragon” Chacho, Omega, Rave, The Brock, Barbwire, Hunter, and White Fire — a cumulative tally with no dates or order recoverable among them. A later, undated Fall 2000 in-fiction magazine names Fury as “the new TV champion,” risen through the fed’s own Hardcore ranks. A further undated predictions column (circa December 2000) has Beorn challenging Joseph for the same title; no document survives naming a winner or dating either change.

name: SWA Tag Team Title
epitaph: The fed's own Wrestler Records page (27 August 2000) credits two wrestlers with one Tag Team Title reign apiece — Hendrickson Tyler and Stevie Paginello, each with an unnamed partner — a cumulative tally with no dates, order, or pairings recoverable. The tag team Secret Service (Matt Cross and Will James) is billed "(c)" — current champions — on the fed's own served 27 May 2001 card, roughly nine months later, the title's own last documented reign in the held record.

name: SWA Intercontinental Title
epitaph: The fed's own Wrestler Records page (27 August 2000) credits two wrestlers with one Intercontinental Title reign apiece — John Rotten and Hendrickson Tyler — a cumulative tally with no dates or order recoverable between them. No further document in the held record names the title again.

name: SWA World Title
epitaph: The fed's own Wrestler Records page (27 August 2000) credits two wrestlers with one World Title reign apiece — Judge and Will Anselm — a cumulative tally with no dates or order recoverable between them. By the time of a later, undated in-fiction predictions column (circa December 2000), the belt is billed as the "SWA/AWA unified championship," held by OutKast — the same title, rebranded once the fed's own SWA/AWA partnership deepened, per that column's own words.

name: SWA Canadian Title
epitaph: Never mentioned in the fed's own 27 August 2000 Wrestler Records page, the Canadian Title is live by the time of a later, undated in-fiction predictions column (circa December 2000), which bills Warren Peace as champion and has him defending against Fury; the column separately names a number-one-contender match for the title between Justin Case and Gangsta. No document records a result for either match, or names the title's own first champion.
